audit.why: Emerald+ 51.02% over 3226 games matches the written arc: Graves bullies levels 1-2 and level 6, Singed takes over from Rylai's. Level chart in content win[] and full phases[].side already agree with each other and with the near-even win rate, so no flips proposed. The packet's levelChart column disagrees with both and looks stale.

audit.whatIsWrong: The text claims Graves's ultimate has a shorter cooldown than Singed's 'early'. It does not: Collateral Damage is 100/80/60 and Insanity Potion is a flat 100, so rank 1 is a tie and Graves only pulls ahead at ranks 2 and 3.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon cooldowns in the kit files.
audit.corrected: Both ults are 100s at rank 1; Graves's drops to 80 then 60 while Singed's stays 100, so the ult war swings to him later, not earlier.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction of the matchup was never stated. Mega Adhesive grounds; Quickdraw is a dash. A Graves standing in the glue cannot Quickdraw out, which is the entire reason the W-into-Fling pattern works. Separately, Smoke Screen is repeatedly described as a 'blind' that 'shuts off your auto-damage' — Riot's own text says it 'reduces sight range', i.e. nearsight, with no blind component. Graves's passive is also unused: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units', so a single minion body eats most of his shotgun.
audit.why: Riot descriptions and derived flags: Singed W grounding, Graves E dash, Graves W zone/slow with sight reduction, Graves P projectile that stops on units.
audit.corrected: Mega Adhesive (17s at rank 1) grounds Graves — glue under his feet, then Fling (10s at rank 1); grounded, Quickdraw cannot carry him out. Smoke Screen nearsights, it does not blind. Keep a minion body between you and his shotgun: the four bullets cannot pass through units.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quickdraw is treated as a fixed timer. Riot's text: 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill and refreshes the resistance boost.' A Graves farming with autos has it back far sooner than 16s.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon description for Quickdraw.
audit.corrected: Quickdraw is 16s at rank 1 but his basic attacks refund it — count his auto hits, not the clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: The pre-run missing-interactions file claims Graves 'can cut your retreat with End of the Line (Q)' via a terrain flag. Riot's description is 'detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain' — End of the Line reacts to terrain, it does not create any. The derived terrain flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire and no wall-cutting advice should be written.
audit.why: Riot description contradicts the derived flag; per instructions the description wins.

edits.before: Graves's Quickdraw dash plus Smoke Screen blind lands at level 2 and he can dash in, burst, and disengage before your Mega Adhesive root animation completes.
edits.after: Quickdraw (16s) and Smoke Screen land at level 2 — the smoke nearsights you rather than blinding, so it is his shotgun burst, not lost autos, that wins the trade.

edits.before: Use Quickdraw to dodge your Mega Adhesive root and disengage every Fling attempt cleanly
edits.after: Dodge the Mega Adhesive throw — inside the glue he is grounded and Quickdraw cannot save him

edits.before: Push early waves fast to deny proxy opportunities and keep you under his tower where Smoke Screen blinds punish your run-pattern
edits.after: Push early waves fast to deny proxy opportunities and keep you under his tower where Smoke Screen's nearsight hides his shotgun angle

edits.before: Graves's E (Quickdraw) and shotgun autos come fully online — he can dash in, burst you, and dash back out before your W-E lands, so avoid extended trades near his auto range.
edits.after: Quickdraw (16s) and shotgun autos come online — his bullets cannot pass through units, so keep a minion between you and half the burst never lands. Avoid open trades in auto range.

edits.before: Collateral Damage wins the raw burst race against Insanity Potion in the immediate 6-6 all-in — use R to survive his ult window rather than to initiate, and proxy the XP lead instead.
edits.after: Collateral Damage wins the raw 6-6 burst race and both ults sit at 100s at rank 1 — spend Insanity Potion to survive his window, not to open one, then proxy the XP lead back.

edits.before:
Level 1 is genuinely even only in the sense that neither of you wants the full commit — but Graves wins any trade you initiate because his shotgun burst and passive armor stacks out-damage early Poison Trail before you have AP. Stay out of his auto range, let the wave push slightly toward you, and do not Fling into his pattern: a Quickdraw dash behind you punishes the cooldown immediately. Your only real tool at level 1 is threatening the proxy — if he zones you off wave, run behind it and collect free XP and gold while he has to choose between stopping you and freezing.

At levels 2-3 his Smoke Screen goes down and blind + burst becomes a lane kill threat. Never run at him in a straight line: his blind shuts off your auto-damage and his shotgun does real burst even through the early armor you lack. Your W-root fling combo can punish an overextended dash, but he has to waste Quickdraw into your glue zone first — at level 2-3 he rarely does. Absorb the poke and start learning his Quickdraw rhythm.
edits.after:

Your only real tool at level 1 is threatening the proxy — if he zones you off wave, run behind it and collect free XP and gold while he has to choose between stopping you and freezing.

At levels 2-3 his Smoke Screen (26s) comes up and nearsight + burst becomes a lane kill threat. Never run at him in a straight line: Smoke Screen only nearsights you — it is the shotgun burst, not a blind, that punishes the straight line. Mega Adhesive grounds, so a Quickdraw ending in the glue cannot leave, but he has to waste Quickdraw into your glue zone first — at level 2-3 he rarely does. Absorb the poke and start learning his Quickdraw rhythm.

edits.before:
Levels 4-5 are the hardest window because Graves is strong, has two item components, and your proxy is the only thing preventing him from running you out of the lane. Ghost toward his second wave camp and run Poison Trail through it — he has to sprint back or lose two waves, and sprint means Quickdraw is committed to a chase rather than a trade. When he chases through the poison, throw W ahead of his path and E him back toward your tower: that is the only trade you are taking before Rylai's.

Level 6 looks like your power spike but Collateral Damage wins the immediate burst race — do not use Insanity Potion to go even on an all-in. Use it defensively when he has burst loaded, let the stat dump eat his damage, and immediately start the proxy loop again. His ult has a shorter cooldown than yours early, so trading ults in a straight 1v1 still favours him. Play the map, not the duel.

Did not act on it.
